ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the image there are two adjacent ordinary dice. The die on the left has a visible top face of 1 dot and a front face of 2 dots; the die on the right has a visible top face of 4 dots, a front face of 6 dots, and a right side face of 2 dots. Then reason: The total number of dots on all faces of an ordinary die is 1+2+3+4+5+6=21, so the total number of dots of two dice is 42. The sum of the dots visible in the image is 1+2+4+6+2=15, therefore the sum of the dots that cannot be seen is 42-15=27.

method.method_draft: First read the visible dice faces from the diagram: the left die shows 1 on top and 2 on the front; the right die shows 4 on top, 6 on the front, and 2 on the right side. From the text, note there are two ordinary dice, so each die has faces numbered 1 through 6, totaling 21 spots. Two dice have 42 spots in all. Add the visible spots, 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15, then subtract from the total: 42 - 15 = 27.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the left die visibly has top face 1 and front face 2; the right die visibly has top face 4, front face 6, and right face 2. Use the ordinary-die rule that opposite faces sum to 7. For the left die, the hidden bottom face is opposite 1, so it is 6; the hidden back face is opposite 2, so it is 5; the remaining two hidden side faces must be 3 and 4. Thus the left die contributes 6 + 5 + 3 + 4 = 18 unseen spots. For the right die, hidden faces are opposite the visible 4, 6, and 2, giving 3, 1, and 5, for 9 unseen spots. Total unseen spots are 18 + 9 = 27.
